chunk_findings.detail: `_is_trivial` delegates to `diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, changed_paths(repo, it))`, but `changed_paths(repo, it)` is the committed-diff path list and does not include untracked files in the dirty tree under test. A tree whose tracked diff is docs-only, but which also contains an untracked `new_feature.py` with real code changes, will be classified as trivial: the new logic file is not among the paths passed to `diff_is_trivial`, so `_selectable` returns `"a trivial change (...)"` and the full suite is skipped, leaving that code untested. The earlier fail-closed dirty-tree fix only covers tracked paths, not untracked ones.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:_is_trivial

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_trivial` classifies the item with `W.repo_root(tree)` and then `diff_is_trivial`, whose dirty-tree and AST checks use that repo's `HEAD` (the same `git diff HEAD` path the prior `[a].py` fix describes). In a linked worktree, `HEAD` is the main checkout, not `tree`. Given main clean at base with `foo.py` as `x = 1`, and the item worktree holding a format-only commit plus an uncommitted `x = 1` → `x = 2` in `foo.py`, `changed_paths` still lists `foo.py`, the dirty check against main is empty, and the change is treated as trivial, so `_selectable` returns a scoped run for a logic edit. Pass `tree` (the tree under test) into `diff_is_trivial`, not the main worktree.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix only preserves the `partial` outcome value. According to the bug, `record_measured` overwrites the existing gate record (that is how `unavailable` erases the baseline-red evidence). The new branch returns `prior` but supplies a brand-new no-tree reason and no copied evidence/reason, so after the reproduced sequence (`gate record T1 unit_tests --outcome partial --reason "baseline red"`, merge, later commit, `gate run T1 unit_tests`) the stored baseline-red reason/evidence is still replaced by the new message. `ddflow approve T1 unit_tests` can still fail because the only acceptable evidence is gone. The regression test checks only `_gate(repo, "unit_tests").outcome == "partial"` and the message text, never that the baseline-red evidence/reason survived, so it would pass even though the destructive erasure the bug is about remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_tree.py:167 and tests/test_gate_run_after_merge.py:test_a_merged_partial_is_kept_not_overwritten_as_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch treats every prior `partial` as settleable by ``ddflow approve {item} {gate}``. The bug statement itself says `gate_accept.refusal` accepts only baseline-red evidence. Given a merged item whose recorded partial is something else (for example `gate record T1 unit_tests --outcome partial --reason "flake, rerun later"`, then a later commit on the base so `item_tree` is empty), `gate run` now keeps the partial but tells the agent the only settlement is `ddflow approve T1 unit_tests`, which that refusal rejects. That is the same class of wrong advice this change removes for `gate record --outcome passed`: the run cannot be re-measured, and the printed command cannot close it. The regression test only plants `--reason "baseline red"` and checks the substring `a person can settle`, so it never catches a non-baseline partial or whether the evidence `approve` actually reads survived.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_tree.py:167

chunk_findings.detail: `_py_ast_equal` compares only `ast.dump(ast.parse(...))`, which erases concrete syntax beyond whitespace/comments. For example a committed diff from `x = 1` to `x = 0x1` (or `x = "a" "b"` to `x = "ab"`) changes the code, but both sides dump as the same `Constant(value=1)`/`Constant(value='ab')`. `_ast_unchanged` then returns True, `_is_format_or_comment` calls it format-only/comment-only, and `diff_is_trivial` drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`, even though the diff edits code and is outside the allowed format/comment classes. That violates the gate contract that a logic/code change is never trivial.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_py_ast_equal

chunk_findings.detail: The “uncommitted edits fail closed” check is scoped to the `paths` argument (`git diff HEAD -- :(literal)<path>`). A worktree whose committed diff is a comment-only edit to `foo.py` (`paths == ["foo.py"]`) but which also has an **uncommitted** tracked logic edit to `bar.py` (`x = 1` -> `x = 2`) is not detected: the diff command for `foo.py` is empty and `_ast_unchanged` compares only `foo.py`, so `_is_format_or_comment` returns True. `diff_is_trivial` then marks a dirty tree containing a logic change as trivial, skipping review and full CI. The whole-tree dirty status, or a diff check not restricted to `paths`, is required.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_format_or_comment

chunk_findings.detail: The new trivial path calls `diff_is_trivial(item, cfg, repo, paths)` with the path list produced by the `diff` callable. In `pipeline_diff.py`, that callable is `lambda: changed_paths(repo, item)`, and `changed_paths` excludes untracked files from the dirty tree under test. So a worktree whose tracked diff is only a format-only change to `foo.py`, but which also contains an untracked `feature.py` with real logic changes, has `paths == ["foo.py"]`; `diff_is_trivial` sees only the format-only `foo.py` and returns true, so `pipeline_by_diff` selects `_trivial_pipeline(gates)` and skips full cross-family review and whole-suite CI even though behavior-changing code is present. The same untracked-file hole was fixed in `testscope._is_trivial` by checking for non-state untracked files before calling `diff_is_trivial`; this new caller does not have that guard.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:pipeline_by_diff

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed fix for previous finding 1 is not sufficient. The new untracked-file guard forces `_is_trivial` to return `False`, but it does not force `test_scope` to run the full suite. With `cfg.gates.unit_tests_small_lines > 1`, a tree whose tracked diff is a one-line comment change in `foo.py` plus an untracked `new_feature.py` gives `lines == 1`; `_is_trivial` is `False` because of the new guard, so `_selectable` falls through to the existing small-task branch and returns `"a small task (1 changed lines < ...)"`. `test_scope` then returns `_selected(...)`, i.e. scoped tests, not `Scope("full")`, so the untracked logic file the guard was added to catch can still skip the whole suite. The regression test named `..._is_not_trivial` only asserts `_is_trivial` is false and does not catch this fallthrough.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:_is_trivial

chunk_findings.detail: `_trivial_declaration` and the review-skip at the `diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, paths)` guard both classify from `changed_paths` only. The untracked-file guard that closed the prior testscope hole lives in `_is_trivial`, not in `diff_is_trivial`. A tree whose committed diff is docs-only, plus an untracked `new_feature.py`, still gets `v.trivial` set and skips rubber_duck, critic, and full ci on the completion path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:_trivial_declaration

chunk_findings.detail: `diff_is_trivial` treats the caller’s path list as the whole change. Docs-only returns immediately, and `_is_format_or_comment` only runs `git diff HEAD -- :(literal)<those paths>` before comparing AST at `base` vs `HEAD`. A committed docs-only or format-only diff plus an unstaged logic edit in another tracked file is therefore trivial. Given `README.md` (or a comment-only `bar.py`) as the only committed path and a dirty `foo.py` of `x = 1` → `x = 2`, both checks ignore `foo.py`, so the function returns True and the trivial tier skips `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`. The earlier untracked-file fix does not cover this: that probe only rejects non-state untracked files, not dirty tracked files outside `changed_paths`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: The untracked-file fail-closed check added in `testscope._is_trivial` is not applied on the pipeline path this change adds. `pipeline_by_diff` classifies from the `paths` callback only, and `pipeline_diff` passes `changed_paths(repo, item)`, which the new comment in `_is_trivial` states does not name untracked work. Given a committed docs-or-format-only diff plus an untracked `new_feature.py` in the item tree, `diff_is_docs_only` or `diff_is_trivial` still sees only the tracked paths, so the item takes `doc_pipeline` or `_trivial_pipeline` and skips cross-family review and whole-suite CI over code that was never classified.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:pipeline_by_diff

data.probe: refuted: ast.dump(ast.parse(...)) equality is the intended 'same behavior' test, not raw-text equality. The examples are semantic no-ops — 1 == 0x1 (both Constant(1)) and 'a' 'b' == 'ab' (both implicit-concat to 'ab') — so classifying them as no-behavior-change is CORRECT, not a missed logic change. A real logic change (x=1 -> x=2) dumps to different Constants and is never trivial; _py_ast_equal/already also guards shebang, mode, symlink and docstring (which IS in the AST).
